messages.author: cb25d91fd630a4e5
messages.subject: Re: Can density be >10?
parts:
This is a common question over at R-help. From the help on hist:

density: values f^(x[i]), as estimated density values. If
all(diff(breaks) == 1), they are the relative frequencies counts/n and
in general satisfy sum[i; f^(x[i]) (b[i+1]-b[i])] = 1, where b[i] =
breaks[i].

So, only if the breaks are of size 1 apart will all density values be
less than or equal to 1. Alternatively, sum(density*bin_width) will
always equal 1, so if you want to plot a histogram such that its scale
matches up with some theoretical probability density function, then
plot density*bin_width.

Mike

parts:
Try this:

prop <- function(x) x / sum(x)
ggplot() + stat_bin(aes(x=dat111, fill= prop(..count..)), binwidth=0.01)

Hadley

messages.author: 969bc1db85a35ba3
messages.subject: Re: Can density be >10?
parts:
I think this is what you want. To get a proportion you need to divide
the count by the total count, i.e. sum(..count..)

dat111 <- rnorm(1000)
p <- ggplot(data.frame(dat111), aes(x=dat111))
p + stat_bin(aes(y=..count../sum(..count..)), binwidth=0.5)

HTH

Gary
